repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgU8Bf564ZGXi4MfHWb

Premise reading (card thread, 2026-11-26T13:42Z): the production-build re-measure the card's first step asks for. Result: all three pages still miss the 2500 ms threshold, so the premise holds and the card stays open. Fix scope is with seat 2 (slice C first in this thread, `Part of` this card).


Tree: objectstack `021524cd` (main). Build: `pnpm build` then `pnpm console:build` (packages/console/dist from the same tree).
Server: `objectstack start` in `examples/app-showcase`, `NODE_ENV=production` (banner: `Mode: production`), sqlite, port 38611,
brotli on (`content-encoding: br` on the document and every asset checked), hashed assets `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
Sign-in: the account signed up over REST, password reset with `os user set-password` (a production server refuses the dev
seed password), then signed in through the Console login form in the same Chrome Lighthouse attaches to.
Tool: Lighthouse 13.6.0 node API, `desktop-config.js` as shipped (formFactor desktop, rttMs 40, throughputKbps 10240,
cpuSlowdownMultiplier 1, mobile false, disableStorageReset false), performance only. Chrome for Testing 158.0.8127.36
headless, 4-core cloud container. 5 runs per page; every run's finalDisplayedUrl is the requested page (not /login), the
LCP element is page content, script requests carry transferSize above 0.

Note: on this boot `/_console/home` lands on `/_console/apps/com.example.showcase/page/showcase_capability_map` and the
list/record URLs redirect to `/apps/com.example.showcase/...` (the app's package id), same pages as the baseline.

## Reading (ms)

| Page | Runs | Median | Dev baseline (#37398) | Threshold |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Home | 3639, 3626, 3538, 3509, 3685 | **3626** | 3557 | 2500 |
| Object list | 4595, 4611, 4483, 4664, 4771 | **4611** | 4625 | 2500 |
| Record page | 4223, 4238, 4285, 4168, 4188 | **4223** | 4175 | 2500 |

The production build changes nothing material: all three still miss, by 45% / 84% / 69%.
Even the login page (an unauthenticated run) reads 2.85–2.90 s.

## Where the time goes

Counterfactual runs (same pages, 2 runs each, one throttling knob changed):

| Page | As shipped | Bandwidth unlimited (RTT 40) | RTT 1 ms (10 Mbps) |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Home | 3626 | 1678–1763 | 2570–2778 |
| List | 4611 | 2367–2516 | 3534–4092 |
| Record | 4223 | 2050–2051 | 3009–3360 |

- **Bytes are ~2 s of every page**: 2.2–2.7 MB transferred before LCP; 1,951 KB of it is the eager JS closure, the same
  120 chunks on every page (the login page included). Largest eager chunks (gzip): vendor-objectstack 684 KB
  (`@objectstack/spec` zod modules — view/dashboard/object/flow/action — plus formula and client), ui-components 351 KB,
  index 131 KB, framework 89 KB, vendor-react 80 KB, i18n-locale-en 71 KB, vendor-radix 58 KB.
  A probe build marking zod builder calls pure (`treeshake.manualPureFunctions: ['z']`) saved only 13 KB: the spec code in
  the eager closure is reached, not dead, so it only shrinks by changing what the shell imports eagerly.
- **Route lazy JS before LCP**: list +491 KB (plugin-grid 192, i18n-ns-studio-en 69, plugins-views 59, ObjectView 33);
  record +388 KB (plugin-grid 192, i18n-ns-studio-en 69, RecordDetailView 35).
- **Round trips ~0.5–1 s**: after the JS lands (~0.7 s observed), the list's data request is issued only after about seven
  serial API rounds (permissions/i18n/org → meta/app → me/apps + meta/object → app bundle + localization → agents +
  meta/view → personal_view → data), observed at 2.27 s.
- **Main thread**: script evaluation 1.1 s (home) to 1.8 s (list, record), mostly attributed to vendor-react (render work);
  observed (unthrottled, local) LCP is already 2.0 / 2.6 / 2.5 s.

Even with unlimited bandwidth the list page sits at ~2.4–2.5 s, so no single seam gets all three pages under 2.5 s.

repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgU8Bf564ZGXi4MfHWb

Correction · card thread of seat 2 · 2026-11-26T22:23Z. Correction to the production reading above (comment 7193730951), plus a reading over HTTP/2.

**Correction.** The line "round trips ~0.5–1 s … about seven serial API rounds before list data" was measured in wall-clock time in a real browser. It is not part of the Lighthouse reading.

- The desktop preset simulates throttling, and its dependency graph does not treat a `fetch()` answer as an edge.
- On the list page, +1500 ms on the one API round that actually holds the data request moved observed LCP by +1.2 s. The Lighthouse median went 4719 → 4621.
- Only one API round after the JS lands holds the list's data (permissions, organization list and auth config, already sent in parallel).

Details are on #37574, closed as not planned for this reason.

**HTTP/2 reading.** Same tree (`9476092c`), same server and Console build, same Lighthouse desktop preset. The only change is that requests go through a local HTTP/2 TLS front. The control row uses the same front with Chrome's HTTP/2 turned off, so the proxy hop is in both rows. Brotli bytes pass through unchanged.

| Page | HTTP/2 (5 runs) | Median | HTTP/1.1, same front (3 runs) | Median |
|:--|:--|--:|:--|--:|
| Home | 2166, 2383, 2297, 2353, 2237 | **2297** | 3691, 3662, 3689 | 3689 |
| Object list | 2686, 2875, 2683, 2837, 2878 | **2837** | 4788, 4748, 4899 | 4788 |
| Record page | 2685, 2586, 2692, 2678, 2788 | **2685** | 4491, 4309, 4296 | 4309 |

- The protocol accounts for 1.4–1.9 s of every page's reading. The earlier readings were all taken over plain-HTTP localhost, which is HTTP/1.1. The simulation charges each of the list's ~150 script requests a round trip on six connections there, and multiplexes them over HTTP/2.
- Over HTTP/2, home already passes 2500 ms. The list misses by ~340 ms and the record page by ~185 ms.
- Script bytes before LCP are unchanged (1923 / 2274 / 2179 KB).

**What this means for the remaining slices.**

- The threshold reading should name its protocol. A TLS deployment is normally HTTP/2, so HTTP/1.1 readings overstate the gap by about 1.5 s.
- Over HTTP/2, the gap that is left is a few hundred ms on the list and record pages. #37572 (eager JS bytes) and #37575 (render CPU) are both sized against that gap now, not against 1.5–2 s.
- The list's two route-lazy chunks before LCP (plugin-grid 192 KB, plugins-views 59 KB) and its 1.8 s of script evaluation are the next places to look.

From now on, this card's LCP acceptance reading is taken over HTTP/2 TLS, and the HTTP/1.1 numbers are listed beside it as a control.

Why: a real deployment serves the Console over TLS, which is normally HTTP/2. The earlier readings were taken on plain-HTTP localhost, which is HTTP/1.1. There, Lighthouse's simulation charges each of the ~150 script requests a round trip on six connections, and that adds 1.4–1.9 s per page that a deployed Console does not pay (comment 7204645317).

Method: the #37444 method unchanged, with the production server behind a local HTTP/2 TLS front. The HTTP/1.1 control uses the same front with Chrome's HTTP/2 turned off, so the proxy hop is in both rows.

HTTP/2 baseline at `9476092c`: home 2297, list 2837, record 2685 ms. Next slice: #37575 (render CPU).

The maintainer (Sales) answered 「同意」 (2026-11-26 23:53Z) to: first-screen LCP readings are taken over HTTPS with HTTP/2, written into this card's acceptance, and the deployment docs state that HTTP/2 is the recommended setup. Reason as put to the maintainer: hosted and production deployments serve HTTP/2; on plain-HTTP HTTP/1.1 the ~150 script requests queue on six connections, about 1.5 s a user on a real deployment does not meet.

**Done when (replaces the card's section of that name):** on a production build served over HTTPS with HTTP/2, under the other conditions of ruling 7178954860 (cold cache, signed in, desktop Chrome, Lighthouse desktop preset, median of 5), the median LCP is at most 2500 ms on home, an object list and a record page. Each reading names its protocol; an HTTP/1.1 reading is a control only. The run is recorded against `ux-conventions.first-screen-lcp`, whose steps carry the protocol condition.

Reading at that condition (local HTTP/2 TLS front, production build): home 2297 ms (passes), list 2837 ms, record 2685 ms. List and record still miss by about 0.2–0.3 s; slices continue in #37575 and #37572.

repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgTd1y1ncyDVcgVtep5

Reading · card thread of seat 2 (#37575 slice 2) · 2026-11-27T08:46Z. Draft PR #37883 (Part of #37575, Part of #37444), which removes first-render re-render passes in the grid and the shell.

**Method:** the #37444 protocol. Production console build, `objectstack start` with `NODE_ENV=production`, local HTTP/2 TLS front, Lighthouse 13.6.0 desktop preset, signed in, cold cache, 4-core container, 10 runs per page. `main` and the PR were built and measured back to back in the same session. The container read about 90 ms slower than earlier in the day, so only same-hour pairs are comparable.

Median LCP in ms:

| Page | `main` 10284387 | PR #37883 | Δ |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Home | 2248 | 2170 | −78 |
| Object list | 2755 | 2700 | −55 |
| Record page | 2608 | 2563 | −45 |

The list and record pages are still over 2500 ms, so #37575 stays open.

**What the profile says is left.** On the list page Lighthouse counts about 2.0 s of script evaluation, almost all React render work. The main thread is busy from about 600 ms until the paint. Before this PR, components re-rendered before the rows mounted outnumbered components mounted about 2.4 to 1. After it, about 6,000 re-renders and 3,900 mounts happen before the rows. Most of what remains is content arriving for real: translation bundles, and object labels as the metadata store fills. The metadata store's single global version counter re-renders every metadata reader on each bump, and a list page sees 6 bumps. Giving the store per-reader selectors is the next lever on this card, and it is an L-size change in `app-shell`.
